messages:
sam: Kicking off canary flip to v2 in us-west-2 at 08:23. Canary pods are Pending with GPU requests, autoscaler not provisioning new nodes. Started a rollback but the traffic-shift job is stuck in 'drain' state. Anyone seeing capacity alerts for that region?

anita: Yep, seeing a bunch of `InsufficientInstanceCapacity` for g4dn/g5 pools in us-west-2. Looks like spot pool got preempted across AZs.

mike: Oof. Are we using spot for the canary nodepool? We usually enable on-demand fallback for the first 5-10% of traffic.

sam: We switched the canary pool to mixed (spot preferred) last week to save $$, guess it bit us. Traffic-shift job output: 
```
$ redwoodctl traffic shift --id canary-20260318
status: draining
progress: 0/10 routes moved
error: pod(s) not ready for routing: 3 pending (InsufficientInstanceCapacity)
```

julia: We can patch the deployment to temporarily reduce GPU resource requests to 0.5 if the model supports it, or move canary to the on-demand nodepool. Quick patch: 
```yaml
# patch snippet
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: model
        resources:
          requests:
            nvidia.com/gpu: "0.5"
```
Not ideal but buys time.

ops-bot: Infra alert: terraform drift detected in module "canary-nodepool": desired_capacity=0 != expected 2. Latest apply failed: quota exceeded for subnet-usw2-a.

anita: Subnet quota hit could be our root cause — provider returned ENOSUBNETS when ASG tried to grow. We hit a provider-side quota in one AZ, autoscaler didn't try other AZs because nodeAffinity restricts to a single AZ for that pool.

mike: Can we relax nodeAffinity for canary nodepool? That would allow cross-AZ provisioning and reduce failure surface. Small change to tf: set `allowed_topology` to regional instead of az. 

eng-pipeline-bot: GitOps sync error on repo `infra/terraform`: helm_release.canary: rollback prevented due to values mismatch in cluster. Manual intervention required.

sam: I don't want to merge infra changes that expand pools mid-rollout. Proposed immediate actions: 1) Pin canary traffic to 0% (abort shift), 2) scale down canary ReplicaSet, 3) open incident, 4) run a one-off on-demand launch in us-west-2 to validate capacity. Thoughts?

julia: +1 to abort shift and scale down. I'll prepare a short-lived patch to nodeAffinity and a tensorflow-lite fallback config if we need reduced GPU.

anita: Also recommend modifying our CD pipeline to detect `InsufficientInstanceCapacity` and automatically flip to on-demand fallback for canary ASGs. File a ticket if you want me to own it.

mike: I'll open an incident and tag infra and platform. We should attach the terraform plan snippet and autoscaler logs.

sam: ok locking the canary and scaling down now. Posting incident: https://redwood.incidents/INC-4821. Incident summary: canary rollout blocked by spot pool capacity + subnet quota + AZ-restricted nodeAffinity => traffic-shift stalled.

ops-bot: Action taken: canary traffic aborted by sam at 08:31. ReplicaSet scaled to 1.

sam: Thanks everyone. Next steps: anita to evaluate changing pool topology and adding quota checks to infra CI; mike to lead postmortem and cost tradeoffs (on-demand vs spot for canaries); julia to test reduced-GPU fallback. Holding rollout until infra changes are validated. :thumbsup:

mike: noted, creating postmortem draft and cost estimate. Will include a short runbook for manual on-demand fallback during urgent rollouts.

julia: I'll run a quick canary with reduced resources on a dev cluster and post results by EOD.

sam: Closing thread — keep updates on incident INC-4821."
